prompt_payload.task: Design a diverse library of executable semantic optimization skills for finite-pool scientific search. Each skill defines interpretable rule features plus a conservative Bayesian linear surrogate blended with strong target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI anchors.

target.title: Dreher-Doyle Buchwald-Hartwig HTE replay
target.boundary: Field values and counts are public; target outcomes are not included.

source_transfer_evidence.boundary: Only source identity, objective, and public source-target field alignment are provided. Source outcomes, effects, support counts, and value priors are withheld.

executor.semantic_model: Rules become binary features. Revealed target outcomes fit a ridge Bayesian linear surrogate whose coefficient prior follows rule weights.
executor.anchor: A rank blend of target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI.
executor.fusion: semantic_mass_start/end controls the rank mass assigned to the semantic surrogate; the remaining mass stays on the target-only anchor.
executor.selection: Independent calibration seeds select one frozen skill. Independent held-out seeds are evaluated only after selection.

design_requirements: Use only exact field/value pairs in public_semantic_fields.

Each conditions object must map a real catalog field name directly to one exact catalog value, for example {"dominant_family": "oxide"}. Never use literal placeholder keys such as exact_field, field_name, field, or value.
Give every skill a distinct, descriptive scientific skill_id. Never copy schema placeholders such as short_unique_name or add numeric suffixes to a placeholder.
Give every skill 3-10 rules; use two-condition interactions only when scientifically meaningful.
Include at least one conservative low-semantic-mass skill.
Include at least one skill grounded only in the supplied source-target field alignment; do not imply that source outcome effects were observed.
Include at least one domain-knowledge skill.
Include a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses or downweights an uncertain source relation.
Prefer mechanistic, chemically or physically interpretable rules over arbitrary coverage rules.
Use positive weights for conditions expected to improve the target objective and negative weights for risks.
Do not claim access to target outcomes and do not output candidate identifiers.

rules.rationale: short scientific rationale

skills.hypothesis: what this skill transfers and when it may fail

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: source_schema_only to real_chemlex_acidamine
cards.summary: The router selected GP-UCB; the descriptive held-out strongest target portfolio remained higher on the 20-seed development range.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: real_suzuki_miyaura to real_buchwald_hartwig
cards.summary: All evidence modes failed calibration and fell back to the target acquisition portfolio.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: real_suzuki_miyaura to real_buchwald_hartwig
cards.summary: Source-schema and target-only LLM strategies failed calibration; the router selected GP-UCB.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: target_only_schema to real_matbench_log_kvrh
cards.summary: No LLM strategy passed calibration; the selected GP-EI anchor did not beat the held-out target portfolio.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: minimize_nitrogen_content_in_acid
cards.summary: For real_chemlex_acidamine, keep the LLM-defined minimize_nitrogen_content_in_acid rule as a bounded fixed prior blended with the target-only optimizer.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Execution: direct_prior. Reusable lesson: target calibration can decide that a fixed semantic prior is more reliable than re-fitting its direction.

cards.title: BH-to-Suzuki confidence-discount transfer
cards.summary: Near-domain transfer plan from Buchwald-Hartwig factor evidence to Suzuki-Miyaura replay.
cards.content: Proposed transfer path: learn public factor evidence from Buchwald-Hartwig, abstract it into a support/confidence card, discount by reaction-domain distance, apply only bounded adjustments in Suzuki, and let the evidence gate authorize or reject each challenger. Compare no-transfer baseline versus transferred-skill-plus-gate on matched seeds.

care_knowledge_context.instruction: Use these public, previously archived cards only as reusable design lessons. Do not copy reported target values into a rule and do not imply that the current target outcomes were observed. Prefer lessons that survived held-out calibration.

rules.rationale: High ligand molecular weight may reduce solubility and slow oxidative addition.
Phosphazene bases are strong, non-nucleophilic bases that may enhance deprotonation.
Iodide is a better leaving group, typically leading to faster oxidative addition.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers source field alignment (acid->aryl_halide, reagent->base, solvent->additive) as a weak prior, assuming similar functional roles. May fail if electronic or steric effects differ substantially between reaction classes.

rules.rationale: Heteroaromatic rings can coordinate to the palladium catalyst, potentially facilitating oxidative addition.
Bromide balance of reactivity and stability may synergize with heteroaromatic coordination.
Moderate additive polar surface area may improve solubility without excessive catalyst poisoning.

skills.hypothesis: Prioritizes candidates with heteroaromatic halides and bromide leaving groups, grounded in mechanistic coordination chemistry. May fail if heteroatom poisons the catalyst or if steric hindrance dominates.

rules.rationale: Guanidine bases are strong organic bases effective for deprotonation in C-N coupling.
Moderate base molecular weight may balance solubility and basicity.
High polar surface area additives may coordinate strongly to Pd, inhibiting catalysis.
Moderate aryl halide size may avoid steric hindrance during oxidative addition.

skills.hypothesis: Emphasizes strong guanidine bases and avoids high-polarity additives, based on domain knowledge of Buchwald-Hartwig mechanisms. May fail if specific ligand-additive interactions override general trends.

rules.rationale: High ligand mass may indicate bulky ligands that could slow reductive elimination.
Low base polar surface area may improve organic phase solubility.

skills.hypothesis: Minimal semantic prior with strong ridge regularization, heavily relying on the target-only GP-UCB anchor for exploration. May fail if weak rules are misleading, but anchor protects against negative transfer.

rules.rationale: Counter to possible source transfer, higher ligand MW may enhance stability in BH vs. acid-amine.
Phosphazene bases may be too sterically hindered for effective deprotonation in BH, reversing source alignment.
Chloride is a poor leaving group in Pd-catalyzed couplings, likely detrimental despite source mapping.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses or downweights uncertain source-derived relations (e.g., phosphazene base favorability), hypothesizing different mechanistic demands in BH vs. acid-amine. May fail if source alignment was actually predictive.

rules.rationale: Moderate base polar surface area balances solubility and minimal catalyst interaction.
Mid-range additive polar surface area may optimize reaction medium polarity.
Absence of heteroaromatic rings may reduce side reactions or catalyst poisoning.
Very high ligand molecular weight likely indicates excessive steric bulk, impeding reductive elimination.

skills.hypothesis: Focuses on steric and polarity balance across components, penalizing very bulky ligands and favoring moderate polarities. May fail if specific electronic effects dominate over steric considerations.

rules.rationale: Iodide is the most reactive halide for oxidative addition, maximizing yield potential.
Bromide offers a good balance of reactivity and stability.
High polar surface area additives may strongly bind Pd, severely suppressing catalysis.
Amidine bases may be weaker and less effective for deprotonation compared to guanidine or phosphazene.

skills.hypothesis: Strongly prioritizes iodide halide reactivity and suppresses high-polarity additives, based on fundamental catalytic cycle knowledge. May fail if iodide leads to side reactions or if specific additives are beneficial despite high polar surface area.

rules.rationale: Mapping from source acid role: lower molecular weight may improve reactivity.
Mapping from source reagent role: higher base molecular weight may correlate with stronger bases.
Mapping from source solvent role: moderate polar surface area may be generally favorable.

skills.hypothesis: Uses only the supplied source-target field alignment (acid->aryl_halide, reagent->base, solvent->additive) to define weak priors, without assuming observed source effects. May fail if the functional role mapping does not translate to similar property-yield relationships.
